title: RBACv2 principal resolution drift — investigation, runbook updates, and SLO recalibration
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
During a spike in SSO token renewals on 2026-02-26 we observed a class of incidents where RBACv2 principal resolution returned stale or duplicate principal IDs for a subset of sessions. This caused intermittent elevation-of-privilege symptoms (admin views visible to a small fraction of users) and a flurry of access-denied noise for legitimate admins. Initial detection came from a Dashboard alert (auth.audit.admin-anomalies) that crossed threshold at 03:14 UTC.

Scope and impact:
- Affected surface: RBACv2 principal mapping service (identity->principal cache + resolution pipeline) and the audit trail linking session tokens to resolved principals.
- Duration: ~45 minutes of elevated error/noise with tailing reconciliation over 3 hours.
- Customer-facing impact: limited number of customers reported transient admin UI inconsistencies; no data exfiltration detected.
- Internal impact: inflated alert volumes and some manual incident triage overhead.

Root cause hypothesis (validated):
A race condition in the principal cache invalidation path when upstream SSO token refresh events and background identity-sync reconciliations coincided. The cache eviction path used a best-effort tombstone which, under concurrent refreshes, could leave two distinct principal objects mapped to the same external subject claim for different sessions. The audit sink (which de-duplicates events by principal ID) then attached the wrong principal for a short window.

Short-term mitigations applied during incident:
- Emergency knob: toggled strict principal-version validation in the gateway (feature flag) to require token->principal signature verification before honoring cached mappings. This reduced incorrect mappings to near-zero at the cost of slight latency increase for first requests (~40ms).
- Increased sampling of audit events for admin routes from 1% to 50% to capture more evidence for postmortem.
- Temporary suppression rule added to reduce duplicate-alert noise while we investigated.

Investigation tasks completed so far:
- Correlated Grafana traces with auth-audit logs to identify request patterns that reproduced the drift.
- Replayed identity-sync and SSO refresh load in staging; reproduced the race using a synthetic token churn test harness.
- Isolated the cache code path and added additional logging around tombstone creation and concurrent invalidation.

Proposed long-term fixes (patch + platform):
1) Fix: canonicalize principal object identity using immutable principal_version token (patch submitted). Ensures cache evictions wait for in-flight resolution to finish or explicitly mark entries as conflicted.
2) Hardening: add compare-and-swap (CAS) semantics to principal cache writes to avoid ABA-like swaps under high concurrency.
3) Observability: extend audit logs to include token fingerprint, principal_version, and resolution path metadata (all stored as structured fields) for 30-day retention on admin routes.
4) SLO/Alerting: recalibrate auth.audit.admin-anomalies to be sensitive to unique principal_id churn vs absolute event volume. The new SLO will track "incorrect principal resolutions per 10k admin requests" and set SLO target to 0.01%.
5) Testing: add an end-to-end chaos test that simulates simultaneous SSO refreshes and identity-sync reconciliations every night in staging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Patch merged to main and deployed to canary with telemetry showing elimination of dual-mapping occurrences in canary (target: 0 occurrences in 24h).
- New alert fires on principal-version mismatch rate > 0.005% in canary and prod.
- Audit log enrichment pipeline validated end-to-end (token fingerprint + principal_version persisted).
- Runbook updated with steps to toggle strict-version feature flag, run the synthetic reproduction, and clear temporary suppressions.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Strict validation increases tail latency for some first-party flows; we need to monitor cost and customer latency SLO.
- Retaining richer audit fields increases storage and retention cost; we recommend tiered retention (30 days enriched for admin routes, 7 days baseline for others).

Next steps (owners):
- Diego: finalize and merge CAS patch; coordinate canary deploy (ETA 2026-03-15).
- Priya (SRE): update alert definitions and SLO dashboard; run canary readiness checks (ETA 2026-03-16).
- Maya: author the runbook and audit-enrichment schema PR (ETA 2026-03-18).
- QA: add nightly chaos regression and include a smoke test that asserts no principal duplication (ETA 2026-03-20).
